summary: Sheet-Phase1 'Fund This Project' — Savings Intelligence & Project Funding Engine (namespace /api/hi/funding/* and /api/hi/admin/funding/*) tested end-to-end. Backend: 16/16 pytest cases PASS covering (1) user /config exposes all five classifications with distinct definitions, (2) POST /goals returns plan.target=250, plan.budget=100, remaining_confirmed_gap=150 and GET /goals/{pid} matches, (3) STRICT classification isolation — confirmed 22.40 reduces confirmed_gap by 22.40; expected 15 leaves confirmed_gap unchanged while making likely_gap<confirmed_gap; potential 50 shows separately and reduces NEITHER gap; opportunistic 30 is accepted, surfaces on the plan, and reduces NEITHER gap; invalid classification returns 400, (4) cost-reduction GET returns all four kinds (best_value_alternative/expected, community_used/potential, owned_or_toolshare/expected, phase_scope/potential) with correct classifications, (5) applying owned_or_toolshare for the tool requirement records a saving AND lowers that orchestrator requirement's cost_estimate from 22 -> 0, (6) orchestrator /events includes PROJECT_FUNDING_TARGET_SET, SAVINGS_REWARD_CONFIRMED, and PROJECT_COST_ALTERNATIVE_FOUND, (7) wallet returns month_confirmed/lifetime_confirmed/pending/active_goals and NEVER exposes internal_revenue / reward_amount / revenue keys, (8) cross-user 404 on both GET /goals/{other_pid} and POST /savings for other user's project, (9) admin dashboard exposes confirmed_customer_savings + cost_reduction_savings + active_goals + completion_rate + internal_revenue=0, admin GET /config lists providers kard@phase3, benefithub@phase4, affiliates@phase2, and PUT /config toggling enabled/conservative_forecast/kard_enabled persists across GET. Frontend (mobile 390×844, demo login): My Home /home-intel exposes 'My Savings' row (testID hi-wallet) that opens the wallet screen ($44.80 lifetime confirmed, $0.00 pending, 2 active goals; NO revenue field visible). Guided Projects → open project → 'Fund This Project' card (testID pd-fund) navigates to /home-intel/funding/{id}. On the funding screen, fund-target + fund-budget + fund-save-goal creates the plan; the plan card renders Confirmed / Pending / Expected / Potential (info only) as FOUR SEPARATE lines each with its own $ value plus a divider and the two gaps (Remaining confirmed gap, Remaining likely gap) as distinct lines. 'Lower project cost' tab exposes fund-scan and renders per-option Apply buttons (fund-apply-{id}). 'Log savings' tab: entering 22.40 and tapping Confirmed updates the plan (Confirmed $22.40, Remaining confirmed gap $127.60 = 150-22.40). Confirmed and Potential are visually and numerically separate — never merged. No red screens, no 500s, no crashes.
critical_code_review_comments: funding_engine.py line 231: the ternary `if req.classification == 'pending' else 'pending'` collapses to always 'pending' for the else branch — harmless but reads as dead code; consider simplifying to a single ternary or map for clarity.

funding_engine.py line 236 double-negatives itself: `status if req.classification in ('confirmed','pending') else 'pending'` — for expected/potential/opportunistic the ledger is force-tagged 'pending' which conflates them at the ledger layer even though the plan keeps them separate. Consider mapping expected/potential/opportunistic to a distinct ledger status (e.g. 'forecast' or 'informational') so the immutable ledger mirrors the classification and admins can't accidentally count forecasts as pending.

Frontend /home-intel/funding/[id].tsx only exposes Confirmed and Expected buttons on the Log savings tab. This is fine for phase 1 (aligns with 'lower project cost first'), but pending/potential/opportunistic can only be added via cost-reduction apply. If manual entry of the other classifications is ever needed, expose them behind a small overflow menu.
seed_data_creation: Test suite creates a fresh orchestrator project ('replace kitchen faucet') with a Faucet material ($180) and Basin wrench tool ($22) requirement for the demo user, a funding goal (target 250 / budget 100), and one confirmed ($22.40), one expected ($15), one potential ($50), and one opportunistic ($30) saving. Also registers a throwaway TEST_fund_*@diyhomie.com user for cross-user isolation. UI test additionally created another project + goal via demo login (visible as 2 active goals in wallet).
context_for_next_testing_agent: test_funding_engine.py covers Phase 1 of the funding surface. If Phase 2 (affiliates) or Phase 3 (Kard) lands, extend TestAdmin to verify provider adapters remain inert until keys are set, and add ledger-shape tests for reward_amount vs internal_revenue_amount. Frontend testIDs: hi-wallet, pd-fund, fund-back, fund-target, fund-budget, fund-save-goal, fund-tab-reduce, fund-tab-plan, fund-scan, fund-apply-{optionId}, fund-saving-amt, fund-add-confirmed, fund-add-expected. Login flow: root → 'I already have an account' → 2 inputs → 'Log in'. To trigger cost-reduction options in the UI, the underlying orchestrator project needs at least one requirement added (which /orch-create alone does not do); the backend engine returns options deterministically from orch_requirements.
